skill.name: concise-planning
skill.description: Creates concise, actionable plans for coding tasks with clear scope, ordered steps, and validation items.
skill.summary: Generate focused coding plans with atomic checklist items and practical validation steps.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Both static detections are markdown backticks in SKILL.md, not executable shell or Ruby code. The skill is prompt-only and instructs the assistant to read project context and produce planning checklists. No prompt injection or intent-level abuse was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Read `README.md`, docs, and relevant code files.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 uses markdown inline backticks around README.md as a filename reference. It does not invoke a shell, Ruby backtick execution, or any external command.
Lines 35-56 are a fenced markdown plan template. The backticks delimit documentation text and are not executable shell or Ruby syntax.

content.value_statement: Planning coding work can become vague and hard to execute. This skill turns requests into scoped, ordered checklists with validation steps.
actual_capabilities: Transforms a coding request into a single actionable plan.
Defines in-scope and out-of-scope work for the task.
Creates ordered checklist items with verb-first wording.
Limits clarification questions to blocking unknowns.
Includes validation or testing steps in the plan.
limitations: Does not implement code changes or run tests by itself.
Depends on available project context for file-specific plans.
May make reasonable assumptions when details are missing.
Focuses on coding tasks, not broad business planning.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Change
use_cases.description: Break a feature request into scoped implementation, validation, and rollout steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare Refactoring Work
use_cases.description: Turn a refactor goal into ordered tasks with clear boundaries and test coverage.

use_cases.title: Clarify Bug Fix Scope
use_cases.description: Create a focused checklist for investigation, repair, regression tests, and release notes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a clear checklist.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise plan for this coding task: [describe the task]. Include scope, ordered action items, and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan With Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using known project details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the available project context and create an atomic plan for [task]. Name relevant files when the evidence supports it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Risky Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise plan for [change]. Include assumptions, boundaries, migration risks, tests, and rollback considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Step Delivery
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for sequencing implementation work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ordered implementation plan for [larger goal]. Separate discovery, implementation, validation, and rollout steps.

output_examples.input: Add filtering to the issue list page.
output_examples.output: A scoped checklist covering current list behavior, filter state design, UI updates, API query handling, tests, and rollout checks.
A plan that separates discovery, compatibility checks, middleware changes, regression tests, and deployment review.
An investigation-first plan covering reproduction, logging review, targeted fixes, regression coverage, and release verification.

best_practices: Provide the user request, relevant constraints, and known project context.
Ask for one concise plan instead of a long design document.
Review assumptions before starting implementation work.
anti_patterns: Using the skill when the user wants immediate code edits.
Asking many clarification questions for non-blocking details.
Creating broad plans without scope boundaries or validation.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a concise coding plan with scope, ordered action items, and validation steps.

faq.question: Does it write or modify code?
faq.answer: No. It guides planning before implementation and does not make code changes by itself.

faq.question: Can it use project files?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the assistant to read relevant docs and code before planning when context is available.

faq.question: How many questions will it ask?
faq.answer: It asks at most one or two questions, and only when the missing details block the plan.

faq.question: Is it useful for non-coding work?
faq.answer: It is designed for coding tasks. General project planning may need a different skill.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
